channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Labor Market Is Hotter Than People Think, Says ADP's Richardson
item.description: Nela Richardson, ADP chief economist and ESG officer, says the US labor market appears stable, and is hotter than people give it credit for. She also says on "Bloomberg Surveillance" that overtime hours on manufacturing floors are picking up. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Hochstein Says There's a 'Secret War' in Iran
item.description: Amos Hochstein, a former top energy advisor to President Joe Biden, says there's a secret war going on in Iran. He says oil tankers are still being attacked in the Strait of Hormuz, but there's been no reporting on it. He says President Donald Trump doesn't have many good options left in Iran. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Iran Escalation Makes More Sense After Midterms, Hochstein Says
item.description: A military escalation in Iran “makes more sense” after November’s midterm elections than before those votes happen, a White House energy adviser to former President Joe Biden said Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Ari Natter, Annmarie Hordern, Jonathan Ferro and Lisa Abramowicz

item.title: Rubio Urges Portugal and Europe to Reduce Dependence on China
item.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Portugal and the rest of Europe should not rely on a single country such as China for key goods, as Washington seeks to limit Beijing’s influence in strategic sectors.
item.dc:creator: Eric Martin and Henrique Almeida

item.title: Putin Is Spending a Record $200 Billion on the Ukraine War This Year
item.description: Russia’s military spending is on track to hit a record this year after Vladimir Putin added almost $60 billion to the costs set out in the budget. Greg Sullivan explains. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Brazil Election: Flávio Bolsonaro Surge Attracts Top Finance Minister Names
item.description: Credit Suisse’s former head of investment banking in Brazil. The chief economist at Latin America’s largest investment bank. The ex-head of the central bank. A senior executive at Bank of America Corp.
item.dc:creator: Martha Beck and Rachel Gamarski

item.title: Airlines Cancel Flights to Riyadh After Houthi Attack on Airport
item.description: Airlines are canceling flights to Riyadh after the Houthis struck two airports in Saudi Arabia in recent days, killing three people and injuring dozens.
item.dc:creator: Leen Al-Rashdan

item.title: Slovak Premier Wants Statue Mocking Trump at EU Parliament to Go
item.description: Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico called for the immediate removal of a statue mocking US President Donald Trump from the European Parliament’s premises in Strasbourg.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Hornak

item.title: UK’s Burnham Open to Germany Joining Next-Gen Combat Jet Program
item.description: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he was open to Germany joining the next-generation fighter jet program led by the UK, Italy in Japan.
item.dc:creator: Moira Warburton and Arne Delfs

item.title: Stocks Drop, Oil Rises on Iran Report; TSMC, Samsung Disappoints Investors
item.description: US equity futures drop and oil rises after a report that the White House asked the Pentagon to draw up strike options against Iran that could be executed before the midterm elections. Samsung posts a nearly nine-fold rise in quarterly operating profit, while TSMC’s sales jump 51%, but the results fail to impress investors. Cayla Seder of State Street discusses the shift in investor behavior. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Europe 'Not Well Prepared for Winter' on Energy, Goldman's Della Vigna Says
item.description:
European natural gas prices rose following a report the White House asked the Pentagon to develop strike options against Iran that could be executed before the midterm elections next month.
Michele Della Vigna, Head of Natural Resources Research in EMEA at Goldman Sachs, says Europe is not well prepared for winter in the energy market with risks skewed to the upside.
"In Europe, natural gas drives 60% of the price of power for 60% of the time. And in some countries, the UK, Italy, Germany, for 80% plus of the time. So all of this ultimately feeds through industrial competitiveness and the consumer's disposable income," he said.
Della Vigna discusses the energy market impacts and risks from conflicts in the Middle East on "The Pulse with Francine Lacqua." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Turkey Says It Won’t Deploy Troops for Attacks Under Mecca Pact
item.description: Turkey won’t send troops abroad to carry out attacks under a defense pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Firat Kozok and Selcan Hacaoglu

item.title: Oil Gains as Iran Attack Risks Rise, Le Pen Asserts Control Over Far Right
item.description:
Oil gained after a report that the White House asked the Pentagon to draw up strike options against Iran that could be executed before the midterm elections.
Brent climbed above $102 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate traded near $90. The report in The Atlantic cited two administration officials, and runs counter to a widespread assumption that President Donald Trump would hold off on escalating the conflict with Tehran before the polls next month.
Marine Le Pen has reasserted her hold on the National Rally party since courts cleared her to run for the highest office, with differences over policy and style emerging in public view.
"The Opening Trade" has everything you need to know as markets open across Europe. With analysis you won't find anywhere else, we break down the biggest stories of the day and speak to top guests who have skin in the game. Hosted by Anna Edwards, Guy Johnson and Tom Mackenzie. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Why Pennsylvania Will Serve as an Early Election Day Bellwether
item.description: The country’s biggest swing state could reveal much about the midterms.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Tamari

item.title: Oil Climbs as Trump Reportedly Weighs Iran Strikes Ahead of Midterms
item.description: President Donald Trump is reportedly considering a plan to launch strikes against Iran ahead of the US midterm election, according to The Atlantic. Tyler Kendall has more on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Italy Adopts Meloni’s Electoral Overhaul Ahead of 2027 Vote
item.description: Italy will transform its electoral system after lawmakers approved reforms that Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni’s allies initially pushed to help her reelection odds next year.
item.dc:creator: Donato Paolo Mancini

item.title: French Students Extend Protests After Premier Delays Response
item.description: French students prolonged their protests after Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said his policy response would only come at the end of the month.
item.dc:creator: Ania Nussbaum

item.title: Royal Navy Member Accused of Gathering Secrets for Russia
item.description: A serving member of the Royal Navy has been accused of using his high-level security clearance to gather secrets he intended to hand over to Russian authorities.
item.dc:creator: Upmanyu Trivedi

item.title: Trump Sued by Democratic Party Over Taxpayer-Funded TV Ads
item.description: The Democratic National Committee filed a lawsuit accusing the Trump administration of unlawfully using government money to pay for advertisements lauding the president that have been airing across the US in recent weeks.
item.dc:creator: Zoe Tillman and Madlin Mekelburg

item.title: UK Sees Trump’s Bomber Pullback as Boost for Iran and Russia
item.description: President Donald Trump’s decision to move US B-1B bombers from a UK airbase citing terror threats may embolden Iran and Russia’s use of proxies to carry out sabotage attacks, according to current and former British officials.
item.dc:creator: Alex Wickham, Ellen Milligan and Gerry Doyle
